claims.text: A machine-learning-based approach can be used to design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory high-entropy alloy compositions.
The relevant starting material is a multi-principal-element alloy system with variable composition.
The proposed model is trained on existing HEA compositions and their measured properties.
The intended RHEA applications involve high-temperature and high-stress conditions.
Atomic-scale crystal structure and lattice distortion mediate the targeted alloy properties.
Patterns learned from existing data enable the machine-learning model to predict an optimal RHEA composition.
The predicted composition will provide a 20% increase in strength-to-weight ratio relative to existing state-of-the-art RHEAs.
State-of-the-art RHEA compositions reported in the literature provide the comparison baseline.
The design search is bounded by the compositional space of a multi-principal-element alloy system.
High-quality data available for training HEA machine-learning models are limited.
Bias in the training data may bias the model's composition predictions.
The proposed validation measures strength-to-weight ratio, ductility, and density in machine-learning-selected compositions.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted compositions fail to achieve at least a 15% increase in strength-to-weight ratio over state-of-the-art compositions.
